feasibility_reasoning:
Measured, not inferred: in the fixture HTML (canonical harness) there are 11 fetchPriority="high" elements. The first img is a 180px image.svg at byte 95915. The hero img.eh-img is at byte 133203 (the flag comes from sliderVariants.tsx:378 plus other image widgets). In the what-if, the literal trigger ('img[fetchpriority=high]' load, then decode, then 1 rAF) started the burst at 212-270 ms, before the observed LCP at 439-596 ms. 289-518 KB of JS ended before obs LCP, so LCP stayed at 4.82 s and 3.77 s.

window.load is not safe either. In one run load fired at 375 ms and obs LCP was 393 ms; the burst started at 383 ms and missed the cutoff by about 10 ms.

The parity claim fails as written. The boot set's dictionary URL and widget URLs are server-only by design: rootHead.ts:84-93 explains that a modulepreload in head breaks root identity, and widgetPreloads.ts:4-6 keeps WIDGET_CHUNK_URLS empty on the client. The widget list is also per-document (index.tsx:212-214). TanStack transformAssets can only rewrite href/crossOrigin (start-server-core transformAssetUrls.js:95-140). It cannot drop preloads or replace the manifest's root scripts entry ({type:module, async, src:/assets/index-*.js} in .output/server/_tanstack-start-manifest_v-*.mjs).

The change needs three pieces: a build-time rewrite of the manifest virtual module (empty preloads and entry scripts, so SSR and the dehydrated client manifest agree), out-of-tree injection of the bootstrap and the per-request URL list (serverSsr.injectHtml or server.ts), and removal of the modulepreload emitters (frameworkPreloads.server.ts:14-28, the widget Link hints, dictionaryPreloadLinkHeaderValue).
blocking_issues: Trigger is wrong as written. 'img[fetchpriority=high]' matches the first of 11 high-priority elements (an image.svg thumbnail), and 'decode + 1 rAF' and 'window load' both fired before the observed LCP in the what-if, which kept LCP at 3.77-4.82 s. Key the trigger on the PerformanceObserver 'largest-contentful-paint' entry plus about 50 ms, with load as a fallback that still waits for that entry.

The SSR/client parity design cannot carry the boot set. Dictionary and widget chunk URLs are server-only (rootHead.ts:84-93, widgetPreloads.ts:4-6). It needs a build-time rewrite of the manifest virtual module (transformAssets cannot drop preloads or scripts, transformAssetUrls.js:95-140) plus injection of the bootstrap and URL list outside the React tree.
e2e/boot-home.spec.ts:27-29 and e2e/boot-timing.spec.ts:996-1012 assert entry and dictionary modulepreload in the Link header, and must be rewritten.
Scope the change to public SSR routes that render an LCP candidate. The 27 ssr:false routes, admin/editor and stored-session users should boot immediately.
The TBT coupling is real (what-if TBT 620-2205 ms vs control 273), so this cannot ship without the hydration/html-weight TBT cuts in the same wave.
effect_reasoning:
Canonical harness (fixture, h2, browser warm-up), n=2 mobile, compared with POMIAR control A (FCP 4.07, LCP 4.82, SI 4.07, TBT 273).

Corrected trigger (LCP-entry observer): FCP 1.52 s, LCP 2.27 s, SI 2.28-2.80 s. No JS ended before obs FCP or obs LCP, which confirms the Lantern rule: getFirstPaintBasedGraph drops nodes with endTime or startTime after the cutoff. Net: FCP -2.55 s, LCP -2.55 s, SI -1.3 to -1.8 s.

Literal trigger: median FCP 2.23 s (bimodal), LCP 4.29 s (-0.53 s only).

The claimed -3.6/-2.95/-1.96 s figures came from the retired h1 harness with bot warm-up (control there was 5.04 s) and used a load+setTimeout trigger, not the described one.

TBT rose to 620/2205 ms (corrected) and 801/1145 ms (literal), within A/A noise of up to ±464 ms. The cause: pre-FCP parse tasks now fall inside [FCP, TTI], while TTI_sim stays put because Lantern does not model the wait.

Fixture scores with score.py, at FCP 1.52 / LCP 2.27 / SI 2.4: TBT 273 gives 92, TBT 620 gives 82, TBT 1000 gives 76.

PSI projection. Production doc is 89 KB vs 47 KB on the fixture (about +0.2 s), and origin latency is 238 ms vs 19 ms (+0.2 to +0.3 s). That gives FCP about 1.8 s, LCP about 2.8-3.0 s, SI about 3.8-4.2 s.
- 53 today
- 78 with TBT unchanged at 600 ms

- 86-87 with W1 bringing TBT to 250 ms or less

Desktop: fixture FCP -0.40 s and LCP -0.26 s, which at PSI's 0.6/1.1 s is +1 to +1.5 points at most. Desktop 95 still depends on TBT.

Cheaper alternative: dropping modulepreloads and setting the entry to low priority gives LCP 3.32 s. That is about 1 s (roughly 7 points) worse than corrected C3, so no cheaper change matches it.
corrected_estimate:
With the trigger keyed on the largest-contentful-paint entry plus about 50 ms, mobile on the fixture: FCP -2.55 s (4.07 to 1.52), LCP -2.55 s (4.82 to 2.27), SI -1.3 to -1.8 s, TBT +350 to +900 ms through coupling.

PSI mobile:
- C3 alone: 53 to 68-70 (+15 to +17), or 78 if TBT were held at 600 ms.
- On top of W1 (TBT 250 ms or less, counting the newly exposed parse tasks): 86-90 (+20 to +24 over W1's 66).

Desktop: +0 to +1.5 points.

With the literal trigger as written: LCP -0.5 s only, worth about +2 to +4 points mobile.

Effort is M-L, not M, because it needs a manifest rewrite plus out-of-tree injection.
better_alternative: Keep C3 but change the trigger and the delivery. Trigger: a PerformanceObserver('largest-contentful-paint', buffered) callback, then setTimeout(about 50 ms), with load used only as a fallback that still waits for the LCP entry, first interaction, and a 3 s cap. Delivery: a Vite plugin rewrites the TanStack manifest so root and route preloads and the entry scripts are empty on both SSR and client, and server-side injectHtml carries the bootstrap plus the per-request boot-set URLs (entry closure, dictionary, route component, above-fold widget chunks). Enable it only on public SSR routes with an LCP candidate. Ship it in the same wave as W1 TBT cuts, and re-gate CLS on at least 5 runs.
